Part of #40230.

"JSON object" is not a thing, and "JSON representation" is simply wrong: it returns a "JSON-serializable object".

I am using the exact same wording as JS pages, such as https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/Temporal/PlainDate/toJSON, to explain how it's implicitly called:

The toJSON() method is automatically called by {{jsxref("JSON.stringify()")}} when an InteractionContentfulPaint object is stringified. This method is generally intended to, by default, usefully serialize InteractionContentfulPaint objects during JSON serialization.

Fixes #23740

Specifically I've tried to address

  • Timing-Allow-Origin is needed for CORS and no-cors, it's for cross-origin protection
  • In the case of cross-origin iframes, responseEnd might measure when the iframe finished loading completely with all its subresources, not just the main resource.
  • encoded/decoded body size are CORS-protected rather than TAO protected

The pages weren't to our templates, so some sections moved into a description.

@noamr Is this something you could review? I think I understood this, but I did use Claude a bit for confirmations and it can be deceptive.

items.content_html: I don't know how dogmatic we are in enforcing that readonly properties are marked as readonly, but it's certainly a bug if a page is already using them and there exist readonly properties that aren't indicated as such, because then readers would assume that their absence means they are not readonly.
items.title: Add missing ReadOnlyInline to pages that already use them

items.content_html:
It might be okay for read-only properties to not be marked as such (our guidelines are murky) but it's never okay for non-readonly properties to be marked as such.

Namely:

  • Dictionaries are never readonly (MediaTrackSupportedConstraints)
  • Derived class members are protocols and can never be enforced as readonly (AudioWorkletProcessor.parameterDescriptors)

...others are just typos. They have never been read-only.

items.content_html:
Description

I've added a one-line note that, on Windows, font-family: cursive means Comic Sans MS.

Motivation

It's an unfortunate quirk of the web that Chrome, Edge, Firefox, and Opera all render font-family: cursive using Comic Sans MS on Windows.

MDN indicates that cursive implies that the glyphs would be at least partially connected by joining strokes, but Comic Sans MS doesn't connect any of its glyphs. IMO, Comic Sans MS is not "cursive," at all.

I was caught very much by surprise when I used font-family: cursive and tested on iOS, Android, and macOS, and got Apple Chancery on iOS/macOS and Dancing Script on Android, but got Comic Sans MS on all browsers on Windows. (Comic Sans MS has a casual, comedic vibe. It was very much not what I was going for when I selected font-family: cursive.)

If a note like this had appeared on MDN, it would have saved me some embarrassment.
items.title: Document that `font-family: cursive` is Comic Sans MS on Windows

items.content_html:
Description

Adds a "Channel values outside the output range" subsection to the "Using relative colors" guide, with a worked display-p3 example showing that channel values beyond the output function's range are used as they are, not clamped or gamut-mapped.

Motivation

The guide explains that channel values resolve to <number> values, but not what happens when the origin color lies outside the output function's gamut. Readers who compute rgb() relative colors from wide-gamut origins see values above 255, and a color(srgb ...) serialization, with nothing on the page explaining either.

Additional details

The example is the one @romainmenke suggested in the issue, kept inside the display-p3 gamut as recommended there. Values checked in Chromium 151:

  • rgb(from color(display-p3 1 0.5 0.5) r g b) computes to color(srgb 1.07398 0.462581 0.483011), so r is about 273.86
  • rgb(from color(display-p3 1 0.5 0.5) calc(r - 1) g b) computes to color(srgb 1.07006 0.462581 0.483011)
  • the absolute rgb(272.86 117.96 123.17) computes to rgb(255, 118, 123), clamped

Spec: CSS Color 5, relative color syntax.

Related issues and pull requests

Fixes #32704
Relates to #32004
items.title: CSS relative colors: explain channel values outside the output range
